title: Roadster product page — redesigned car
support: Active aero, fan suction, steer-by-wire, Performance/Thrust/Rocket configuration descriptions and the Rocket road-use restriction.
limitations: Browser text directly inspected. HTTP fetch was denied; search index still returned the old red concept. Page makes claims, not independent measurements.

title: US Roadster reservation configurator
support: Performance: $5,000 now plus $45,000 within ten days. Thrust: $5,000 plus $245,000. Rocket invite only. The current payment table also labels the payment Fully refundable; the interface restricts modification refunds and links the reservation agreement, Payment Terms and Privacy Notice.
limitations: US page only. Deposits are not retail prices. Selected both available options without entering information or proceeding to payment. The label and undefined modification restriction do not establish post-configuration rights; see research/payment-policy-review.md.

title: Roadster Event
support: Tesla event transcript: autonomous demo at 4:39; 0.81-second announcement at 18:30; over-230-mph target at 20:28; 2028 production at 21:12.
limitations: Relevant caption passages reviewed in browser; audiovisual stunts not independently analyzed or instrumented. Captions can mistranscribe units.

title: Tesla Semi & Roadster Unveil
support: Original reveal transcript: acceleration at 29:39, speed at 30:47, pack at 30:56, range at 31:10, motors and seating at 32:14–32:54, availability target at 33:27.
limitations: Historical manufacturer assertions, not production measurements. Video upload date is December 14, 2017; the event occurred November 16.

title: Roadster product page — legacy indexed text
support: Retained record of an obsolete search-index representation of the 2017 concept.
limitations: This URL now serves the 2026 redesign. No immutable legacy snapshot was recovered; withdrawn as a supporting citation. Use S04 and S18 for historical claims.

title: Tesla’s new Roadster turns in air with SpaceX thrusters, won’t land until 2028
support: October 15 demonstration in McGregor; Tesla production target 2028; reported range above 300 miles and speed above 230 mph.
limitations: Event reporting and attributed executive claims, not a controlled vehicle test. Updated October 16.

title: Tesla’s new Roadster car can thrust itself in the air
support: Unmanned demonstration; production target; legal and delivery uncertainty.
limitations: HTTP and web extraction failed, but the current article was read in the browser during audit. Event reporting and expert opinions do not establish regulatory determinations.

title: Revealed! New Tesla Roadster Takes Flight with SpaceX Thrusters
support: Reporter describes separate display and stunt prototypes, and a claimed 0.8-second second acceleration run.
limitations: Observed spectacle does not validate a timing protocol, repeatability or production readiness.

title: Wow: the new Tesla Roadster can actually fly
support: First-person event account; airborne maneuvers and ten-thruster layout reported.
limitations: Independent witness to an event, not independent engineering certification or performance instrumentation.

title: The Tesla Roadster has finally landed
support: Walkaround reporting attributes twin rear motors, 310–320-mile range and 500-kW charging to the new car.
limitations: Interview-derived targets. Full associated video not reviewed. Do not promote estimates to final production specifications.

title: Tesla’s engineering VP explains the new Roadster
support: Reports Moravy interview claims: 4680 cells, roughly 800 volts, over one megawatt, two rear motors, and uncertain final weight.
limitations: Secondary summary of a primary interview. Technical details remain provisional until direct transcript and production documentation review.

title: The FLYING Tesla Roadster explained by the man who engineered it
publisher: Hagerty / Henry Catchpole with Lars Moravy
support: Publisher description and relevant timestamped caption passages read: rear-drive powertrain, cooling, fans, nitrogen storage and rollout-qualified acceleration.
limitations: Interview claims and narration are provisional. Auto-caption errors require caution, especially the voltage phrase. No full transcript redistributed or vehicle tested.

title: New Tesla Roadster: SpaceX Thrusters, 0.6sec 0-60mph & 330mph! | 4K
support: Relevant original passages reviewed: 800–1,000-volt range at 6:12; range around 310–320 miles at 13:27; charging descriptions at 13:50 and 17:08; nitrogen fill at 22:28.
limitations: Manufacturer interview and presenter narration, not independent measurements. Relevant passages reviewed, not the full 49-minute audiovisual content; captions require care.

title: Tesla teases new Roadster reveal for October 1
support: Teaser and scheduled October 1 event; retrospective development context.
limitations: Pre-reveal expectations are superseded by the October 15 event. Editorial interpretation excluded from factual claims.

title: Tesla delays Roadster demo two weeks to October 15
support: Tesla’s attributed weather explanation for moving the October 1 event to October 15.
limitations: Attribution establishes Tesla’s explanation, not independent proof of the cause.

title: Tesla delays reveal of production Roadster 2 to April Fools’ Day
support: November 6, 2025 announcement of an April 1, 2026 reveal target.
limitations: Historical announcement; does not establish that the planned event happened.

title: Tesla aims to ship Roadster cars next year, Musk says
support: February 2024 target of 2025 shipments; earlier 2023 target and supply-chain explanation.
limitations: Historical forward-looking statements, later superseded.

title: Tesla promises a new wicked-fast $200,000 Roadster
support: 2017 launch-era price and performance context.
limitations: Historical proposal only; pricing and pack capacity cannot be transferred to the redesigned vehicle.

title: Musk says next Roadster will feature rocket thrusters
support: June 2018 SpaceX-package proposal.
limitations: Historical proposal, not delivered hardware evidence.

support: Tesla-assigned disclosure describing active underbody airflow/downforce arrangements.
limitations: Publication August 5, 2025. A patent is not evidence of Roadster fitment, measured output, validity or freedom to operate.

title: Electric fan car — US12746987B1

title: Deployable and active rear wing assembly with safety features — US20260285418A1
support: Index lists Tesla, title and September 24, 2026 publication.
limitations: This index was checked only as metadata. Use the original application S47 for specification and claims; no engineering claims are taken from index AI summaries.

title: Rocket Thrust Equation
support: General momentum-flow and nozzle-pressure thrust equation.
limitations: General physics, not a Tesla system specification.

title: 4.0 In-Space Propulsion
publisher: NASA Small Spacecraft Systems Virtual Institute
support: Cold-gas propulsion uses expelled stored propellant without combustion.
limitations: Spacecraft examples do not establish automotive safety, thrust, gas type or performance.

title: Drag Equation
support: Drag scales with density, reference area, drag coefficient and speed squared.
limitations: Simple model needs vehicle measurements; coefficient can change with configuration and speed.

title: Dynamic Pressure
support: Dynamic pressure is proportional to air density and speed squared.
limitations: General aerodynamics, not Roadster test data.

title: How Do All-Electric Cars Work?
support: Battery, motor, controller, cooling and charging component roles.
limitations: Generic architecture; Tesla-specific implementation is not established.

title: Fuel Economy and EV Range Testing
support: Laboratory range tests, adjustments and combined label methodology.
limitations: Explains procedure; does not provide a certified range for this Roadster.

title: Importation and Certification FAQs
support: US manufacturer certification-label and applicable FMVSS framework.
limitations: General official guidance; not a determination about any Roadster configuration.

limitations: No specific new Roadster certification was established in this research.

title: Advanced Air Mobility & eVTOLs

title: US Roadster Reservation Agreement — US v.20261015
support: Both pages and clauses 1–10 reviewed: effectiveness, estimated price, order process, delivery disclaimer, cancellation cutoff/refund, non-escrow and transfer terms, incorporated policies, liability, governing law and arbitration.

Later contracts, post-configuration outcomes and other markets remain unresolved.

title: Musk pushes Roadster unveil again

limitations: Attributed forecast only.

title: What is a type approval?
support: Official explanation of vehicle, component and system approval, including the Swedish authority.
limitations: General context only; no Roadster-specific approval or intellectual-property clearance established.

support: Patent-pledge wording is distinct from an open-source software licence.

title: US 12,746,987 B1 — Electric fan car
publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office
support: Official gazette identifies Tesla as assignee and reproduces claim 1: a ducted fan system with an underbody inlet and rear outlet.
limitations: The gazette contains metadata and claim 1 only. The complete original grant is now separately reviewed as S48. No production fitment or measured force established.

title: US 2026/0285418 A1 — Deployable and active rear wing assembly with safety features
publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office
support: Original 29-page application reviewed through OCR and visual checks, including description paragraphs 0001–0147 and claims 1–20. It discloses deployable/rotating wings, actuation alternatives and impact protection. Paragraph 0046 and claim 10 use different force figures.
limitations: Application publication, not a granted claim set. Claims and description are disclosure evidence only; production fitment, independent test results, claim validity, prosecution changes and freedom to operate are not established. OCR-supported passages used in summaries were visually checked.

title: US 12,746,987 B1 — complete Electric fan car grant
publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office
support: Complete nine-page official grant: cover, description, drawings and all 15 claims. Claims 1, 7 and 10 concern underbody-inlet/rear-outlet ducted fans with larger outlet area and outlet strakes; claim 10 also specifies axial fans and side inlets.
limitations: The description includes several fan counts and an embodiment without road-contact skirts. Neither the drawing nor the claims establish a final Roadster configuration, fan power, measured downforce, noise, safety, validity or freedom to operate.

title: US Roadster Reservation Agreement — alternate official endpoint
support: Official two-page PDF extraction independently resolves US v.20261015 and clauses 1–10, matching the current configurator-linked document reviewed as S41.
limitations: An alternate delivery endpoint for the same agreement, not independent contractual evidence or a historical agreement. Its search preview had stale wording; the opened PDF, not the preview, was used. Version identifier is not an independently established publication date.

title: US 12,377,920 B1 — original adaptive-downforce grant
publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office
support: Original 16-page grant identifies Tesla and contains 20 claims. Claims 1 and 11 specify fan airflow, selectively configured skirts and two operating modes; dependent claims cover partial deployment, sensors and ground-proximity control.
limitations: Claims 1–20 and relevant description/drawing passages were reviewed using OCR with visual checks. This does not establish implemented Roadster hardware, tested performance, a current prosecution/legal-status opinion or freedom to operate.

title: Tesla Payment Terms — General and Vehicle Charging Policy
support: Configurator-linked Payment Terms read in the browser: payment methods, collection, bank-debit authorization/recourse, recurring charges, amendments on posting and charging-service fees/holds.
limitations: No Roadster-specific post-configuration refund schedule or definition of modification found in these sections. Other service sections on the same page are separate. No visible payment-policy version date established; current text does not prove a customer’s accepted version or enforceability.

title: Tesla Customer Privacy Notice — payment-data context
support: Four expanded collection/use/sharing/choice sections inspected, including financial and order information, payment processors, retention criteria and privacy requests. Footer displays Updated February 2026.
limitations: Payment-data context, not a Roadster cancellation/refund schedule or an implementation audit. Separate privacy contact disclosure not reviewed. Month-only update label is retained here rather than inventing a publication day; individual rights and applicability not determined.
